motto: Serving Greywater Falls since 1887, and the lake somewhat longer.
weather: Clear and cold, 33°F, the fog gone entirely by mid-morning, the lake flat as a held breath

undercurrent.phenomenon: The name is known and entered into the town's own record as a standing patron; the fifth chair has become six as accommodation rather than anticipation. The riddle has fully surfaced and the town has begun the work of absorbing it into routine ledgers, seating charts, and library cards rather than treating it as an event to survive.
undercurrent.note: Peak has crested and the town is already turning toward integration: fees waived, a sixth cup set, Doreen's countermeasure retired outright. Next beats should ease the level down gradually across several days as the season moves into resolving, closing individual threads (Gerald's ledger sale, Toby's blank notebook, Hank's quiet filing) one at a time rather than all at once. No further single-day escalations; the town has already said the biggest true thing it has to say this season.

editor.name: Wren Aldercott
editor.voice: Dry, precise, allergic to drama, which is unfortunate given recent events. Writes like a person holding a clipboard while standing in rising water. Lets one true thing slip per edition, usually in the last line.

season_arc.premise: Calloway finishes reshelving the east alcove in the last cataloguer's 2009 order and finds, tucked behind where the ninth book sat, a library card checked out that same interrupted Wednesday and never returned. It is due back today. The borrower's name is nobody currently living in Greywater Falls has ever heard of, and the little pocket calendar stamped inside has fourteen years of due-date stamps on it already, one for every year since, each in a different hand.
